Produces the manuscript's main figures: Fig1 (A-B), Fig2 (A-D), Fig3 (A-D),
Fig4 (A-C), Fig5 (A-B), Fig6 (A-C). Section 18 runs the MixSIAR/JAGS mixing
model, which can take a long time - Fig4 and Fig5 depend on its output.
Supplementary figures are produced separately in Supplementary_figures.Rmd.

#1. Load packages and colour palette

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(Hmisc)
library(ggpubr)
library(googlesheets4)
library(here)
source(here('script','colors.R'))
set.seed(1)  # reproducible geom_text_repel label placement
```

#2. Load data

```{r}
Data  <- read.csv(here('data','Dataset_S1.csv'), fileEncoding = "macintosh")
Data  <- Data %>% filter(!is.na(Sample_ID))  # drop trailing blank rows
humans <- filter(Data, group == "Human")
fauna <- filter(Data, group == "Fauna")
```

#3. Fig1a - map of selected human isotope sites

Site coordinates come from data/Site_coords.xlsx (HUMAN sheet); points are
coloured by Site using colors.R's site_cols/site_order. Country borders
come from rnaturalearth/rnaturalearthhires (bundled locally); topography
and bathymetry are fetched via geodata/marmap and cached after first run.

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthhires)
library(geodata)
library(terra)
library(marmap)
library(ggnewscale)
library(cowplot)
library(ggrepel)

site_coords <- read_excel(here('data','Site_coords.xlsx'), sheet = "HUMAN") %>%
  mutate(Site = trimws(Site), LAT = as.numeric(LAT), LONG = as.numeric(LONG)) %>%
  filter(Site %in% site_order, !is.na(LAT), !is.na(LONG)) %>%
  distinct(Site, LAT, LONG)

x_min <- -50; x_max <- -43
y_min <- -29; y_max <- -23

brazil <- ne_countries(country = "Brazil", scale = "large", returnclass = "sf")

dir.create(here('elevation_data'), showWarnings = FALSE)
# 3 arc-second SRTM tiles mosaiced together; the south-eastern tile is open
# ocean with no SRTM data and 404s, so missing tiles are skipped.
srtm_tiles <- expand.grid(lon = c(-47, -44), lat = c(-26, -22))
topo_tiles <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(srtm_tiles)), function(i) {
  tryCatch(
    geodata::elevation_3s(lon = srtm_tiles$lon[i], lat = srtm_tiles$lat[i], path = here('elevation_data')),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
})
topo_tiles <- Filter(function(t) inherits(t, "SpatRaster"), topo_tiles)
topo <- do.call(terra::merge, topo_tiles)
topo <- terra::crop(topo, terra::ext(x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max))
topo_df <- as.data.frame(topo, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
colnames(topo_df)[3] <- "elevation"

bath <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(lon1 = x_min, lon2 = x_max, lat1 = y_min, lat2 = y_max, resolution = 0.5, keep = TRUE, path = here('elevation_data'))
bath_df <- marmap::fortify.bathy(bath) %>% filter(z <= 0)
depth_breaks <- c(-5000, -4000, -3000, -2000, -1000, -500, -200, -100, -50, 0)
bath_colours <- colorRampPalette(c("#08306b", "#2171b5", "#6baed6", "#deebf7"))(length(depth_breaks) - 1)

map_theme <- theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_line(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.2),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )

legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 6),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 5),
  legend.key.size = unit(0.26, "cm"),
  legend.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA)
)

base_map <- ggplot() +
  # geom_raster (not geom_tile) embeds this as one bitmap; geom_tile would
  # draw millions of vector rects at this resolution, bloating the PDF.
  geom_raster(data = topo_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = elevation)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cde7ca", high = "#4b514a", name = "Elevation") +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_contour_filled(data = bath_df, aes(x = x, y = y, z = z), breaks = depth_breaks, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = bath_colours, name = "Depth") +
  geom_sf(data = brazil, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.08) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(x_min, x_max), ylim = c(y_min, y_max), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-50, -43, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-29, -23, 1))

# Extracted from standalone copies so they can be inset onto the map
# instead of taking space as an external legend column.
elev_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(
  ggplot(topo_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = elevation)) + geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#cde7ca", high = "#4b514a", name = "Elevation") +
    legend_theme
)
depth_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(
  ggplot(bath_df, aes(x = x, y = y, z = z)) + geom_contour_filled(breaks = depth_breaks, alpha = 0.75) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = bath_colours, name = "Depth") +
    legend_theme
)

inset_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = brazil, fill = "#cde7ca", colour = "#4b514a", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = x_min, xmax = x_max, ymin = y_min, ymax = y_max), colour = "red", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = -53, y = -10, label = "Brazil", size = 4, colour = "grey30") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-75, -32), ylim = c(-35, 6), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
    plot.margin = unit(c(0, 0, 0, 0), "pt")
  )

# Rendered to a bitmap (not placed as a ggplotGrob) so annotation_raster
# stretches it to fill its box exactly, rather than letterboxing to its
# own coord_sf aspect ratio.
inset_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
ggsave(inset_png, inset_map, width = 5, height = 4.93, units = "cm", dpi = 300, bg = "transparent")
inset_img <- png::readPNG(inset_png)

human_map <- base_map +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_point(data = site_coords, aes(x = LONG, y = LAT, fill = Site), shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.45, colour = "black") +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = site_coords, aes(x = LONG, y = LAT, label = Site),
    size = 3, colour = "black", seed = 1, nudge_y = 0.3,
    xlim = c(x_min, x_max), ylim = c(y_min, y_max),
    min.segment.length = Inf
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_cols, breaks = site_order) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  map_theme

# Placed by longitude/latitude (not canvas fraction) so they stay clear of
# site points/labels regardless of the figure's final dimensions.
Fig1a <- human_map +
  annotation_custom(elev_legend, xmin = -49.9, xmax = -48.57, ymin = -24.93, ymax = -23.1) +
  annotation_custom(depth_legend, xmin = -44.835, xmax = -43.315, ymin = -28.8, ymax = -26.57) +
  annotation_raster(inset_img, xmin = -47.55, xmax = -45.15, ymin = -28.8, ymax = -26.48)
Fig1a
```

#4. Fig1b - bulk collagen isotopes in the context of previously published data

Dataset_S2.csv compiles previously published bulk collagen isotope data
(Colonese et al. 2014; Pezo-Lanfranco et al. 2018), alongside the samples
selected for this study's CSIA analysis, matched by burial number. Most
sites' Individual entries are formatted "Burial <number>"; Piaçaguera's are
bare numbers (e.g. "5"), so the matching falls back to those directly.

```{r}
S2 <- read.csv(here('data','Dataset_S2.csv'), fileEncoding = "macintosh")

extract_burial <- function(x) {
  sapply(x, function(v) {
    if (is.na(v)) return(NA_character_)
    v <- iconv(v, from = "UTF-8", to = "UTF-8", sub = "?")
    m <- regmatches(v, regexpr("(?i)burial\\s+(\\S+)", v, perl = TRUE))
    if (length(m) > 0 && m != "") return(sub("(?i)burial\\s+", "", m, perl = TRUE))
    v_trim <- trimws(v)
    if (grepl("^[0-9]+[A-Za-z]?$", v_trim)) return(v_trim)
    NA_character_
  }, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

humans_burial <- humans %>% mutate(burial_key = extract_burial(Original_.ID)) %>%
  select(Site, Sample_ID, burial_key)
S2 <- S2 %>% mutate(burial_key = extract_burial(Individual)) %>%
  mutate(used_in_study = !is.na(burial_key) &
           paste(Site, burial_key) %in% paste(humans_burial$Site, humans_burial$burial_key))

Fig1b <- ggplot(S2, aes(x = X_13Ccol, y = X_15Ncol, fill = Site)) +
  geom_point(data = subset(S2, !used_in_study), pch = 21, colour = "grey50", size = 2.5, stroke = 0.3, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(data = subset(S2, used_in_study), pch = 21, colour = "black", size = 2.5, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = site_cols, breaks = site_order) +
  labs(x = expression(delta^{13}*C[collagen]*"(‰)"), y = expression(delta^{15}*N[collagen]*"(‰)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "bottom", limits = c(-25, -5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(position = "left", limits = c(0, 21)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "inside", legend.position.inside = c(0.8, 0.18),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.85), colour = NA),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.36, "cm"),
    plot.margin = margin(2, 2, 2, 2)
  )
Fig1b
```

#10. Fig2d faunal remains fingerprinting

Define reference ranges from primary producer databases.

```{r}
Ref_C <-  read.csv(here('data','C_fingerprinting.csv'))
Ref_N <-  read.csv(here('data','N_fingerprinting.csv'))
Ref_C <- Ref_C %>%  dplyr::select(Group, Category, Code, ile_d13C, leu_d13C, lys_d13C, val_d13C, phe_d13C)
Ref_C <-Ref_C %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(valphe_13C = (c(val_d13C - phe_d13C)))
Ref_C <- Ref_C %>% dplyr::filter(Category == 'C3_terrestrial_plant' | Category == 'phytoplankton' |Category == 'green algae' |Category == 'brown algae' |Category == 'red algae')
Ref_C <- na.omit(Ref_C)


Ref_N <- Ref_N %>%  dplyr::select(Group, Group1, Category, Code, phe_d15N, lys_d15N)
Ref_N <-Ref_N %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(lysphe_15N = (c(lys_d15N - phe_d15N)))
# Group1 folds red/green/brown algae together under Macroalgae.
Ref_N <- Ref_N %>% dplyr::filter(Group1 %in% c('Macroalgae', 'Phytoplankton', 'Terrestrial plants'))
Ref_N <- na.omit(Ref_N)

# Places each category's label where its density curve is tallest relative
# to the others (falls back to its own peak if never tallest anywhere), so
# labels land clear of overlapping neighbours in the Fig2d/Fig3d margins.
find_exclusive_label_pos <- function(data, value_col, group_col, grid) {
  groups <- unique(data[[group_col]])
  dens_mat <- sapply(groups, function(g) {
    vals <- data[[value_col]][data[[group_col]] == g]
    d <- density(vals)
    approx(d$x, d$y, xout = grid, rule = 2)$y
  })
  dominant <- groups[max.col(dens_mat, ties.method = "first")]
  out <- lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) {
    g <- groups[i]
    idx <- which(dominant == g)
    if (length(idx) == 0) {
      # never the tallest curve anywhere - fall back to this category's own peak
      x_pos <- grid[which.max(dens_mat[, i])]
    } else {
      runs <- split(idx, cumsum(c(1, diff(idx) != 1)))
      best_run <- runs[[which.max(lengths(runs))]]
      x_pos <- grid[best_run[which.max(dens_mat[best_run, i])]]
    }
    y_pos <- 0.5 * approx(grid, dens_mat[, i], xout = x_pos)$y
    data.frame(group = g, peak_x = x_pos, peak_y = y_pos)
  })
  setNames(do.call(rbind, out), c(group_col, "peak_x", "peak_y"))
}

grid_C <- seq(-6, 9, length.out = 600)   # matches Ref_C_plot's display window
Ref_C_labels <- find_exclusive_label_pos(Ref_C, "valphe_13C", "Category", grid_C) %>%
  left_join(distinct(Ref_C, Category, Code), by = "Category")

grid_N <- seq(-11, 6, length.out = 600)  # matches Ref_N_plot's display window
Ref_N_labels <- find_exclusive_label_pos(Ref_N, "lysphe_15N", "Group1", grid_N) %>%
  left_join(distinct(Ref_N, Group1, Code), by = "Group1")

# Restricted to a window near Fig2d_base's axis limits so far-outlying
# reference values don't dominate the density curves.
Ref_C_plot <- Ref_C %>% dplyr::filter(valphe_13C >= -6, valphe_13C <= 9)
Ref_N_plot <- Ref_N %>% dplyr::filter(lysphe_15N >= -11, lysphe_15N <= 6)
```

Reference producer category colours come from script/colors.R (`ref_cols` /
`ref_group1_cols`).

```{r}
   scale_fill_manual(values=category_cols, breaks=names(category_cols))+
```

Make the composite Fig2d/Fig3d "big D" plot (main panel + marginal densities).

```{r}
library (ggExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(cowplot)
# axis_canvas() aligns xdens/ydens to Fig2d_base's coordinate system.
xdens <- axis_canvas(Fig2d_base, axis = "x") +
  geom_density(data= Ref_C_plot, aes(x = valphe_13C, fill = Category), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.2) +
  # direction="y" keeps each label's x fixed at its own median, so repel
  # only slides labels vertically to dodge collisions.
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = Ref_C_labels, aes(x = peak_x, y = peak_y, label = Code, colour = Category),
            size = 2.2, fontface = "bold", seed = 1, direction = "y",
            fill = "white", label.size = 0.35, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
            force = 2, force_pull = 0.3,
            min.segment.length = Inf, segment.size = 0.2, box.padding = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ref_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ref_cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
ydens <- axis_canvas(Fig2d_base, axis = "y", coord_flip = TRUE) +
  geom_density(data = Ref_N_plot, aes(x = lysphe_15N, fill = Group1), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.2) +
  # Mirrors xdens; pre-flip keeps peak_x aligned post-flip with Fig2d_base's y-axis.
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(data = Ref_N_labels, aes(x = peak_x, y = peak_y, label = Code, colour = Group1),
            size = 2.2, fontface = "bold", seed = 1, direction = "y",
            fill = "white", label.size = 0.35, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"),
            force = 2, force_pull = 0.3,
            min.segment.length = Inf, segment.size = 0.2, box.padding = 0.25) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ref_group1_cols) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ref_group1_cols) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
# panel_d_scale gives Fig2d/Fig3d's grid cell extra width/height to offset
# the marginal density strips, so D's core panel matches A/B/C's size.
margin_frac <- 0.25  # relative size of the marginal density strip
panel_d_scale <- 1 + margin_frac
Fig2d <- insert_xaxis_grob(Fig2d_base, xdens, grid::unit(margin_frac, "null"), position = "top")
```

#17. Prepare EAA data for the MixSIAR mixing model (Fig4/Fig5)

```{r}
EAA <- Data %>%  dplyr::select(Site, Region, Sample_ID, category, common_name, Group, group, d34S,d13C,d15N, ile_d13C, leu_d13C, lys_d13C, val_d13C, phe_d13C, phe_d15N, lys_d15N)
```

Create a source data file for marine and terrestrial faunal references and
find means and SDs (needed for multiple tracers rather than a 'raw' model).

```{r}
Sources <- EAA %>% subset(group =="Fauna")
Sources <- Sources %>%filter(!common_name == "guinea pig" & !common_name == "armadillo"& !common_name == "coati")

Source_means <- Sources %>% group_by(Group) %>% summarise (Meanile_d13C
 = mean(ile_d13C), Meanleu_d13C  = mean(leu_d13C), Meanlys_d13C
 = mean(lys_d13C), Meanval_d13C = mean(val_d13C), Meanphe_d13C = mean(phe_d13C), Meanphe_d15N = mean(phe_d15N), Meanlys_d15N = mean(lys_d15N), SDile_d13C = sd(ile_d13C), SDleu_d13C  = sd(leu_d13C), SDlys_d13C = sd(lys_d13C), SDval_d13C = sd(val_d13C), SDphe_d13C = sd(phe_d13C), SDphe_d15N = mean(phe_d13C), SDlys_d15N = mean(lys_d15N), n = n())

write.csv (Source_means, here::here("mixingmodel", "Sources.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

#18. Apply the MixSIAR model

Load source data and consumer data.

```{r}
library(devtools)
library(MixSIAR)

#Load mixture data
mix <- load_mix_data(filename=here('mixingmodel','Humans.csv'), iso_names=c("ile_d13C", "leu_d13C", "lys_d13C", "val_d13C", "phe_d13C", "phe_d15N", "lys_d15N"),
                     factors="Sample_ID",
                     fac_random=FALSE,
                     fac_nested=FALSE,
                     cont_effects=NULL)

#Load source data
source <- load_source_data(filename=here('mixingmodel','Sources.csv'),
                           source_factors=NULL,
                           conc_dep=FALSE,
                           data_type="means",
                           mix)
#Load discrimination data including the offsets for the EAAs if required. Note d13C lysine does not have a value.
discr <- load_discr_data(filename= here::here("mixingmodel", "Discr.csv"), mix)
```

Create the JAGS file and run the model (test, then the full "very long" run).

```{r}
model_filename <- "MixSIAR_model.txt"# Name of the JAGS model file
resid_err <-FALSE
process_err <-TRUE
write_JAGS_model(model_filename, resid_err, process_err, mix, source)
```

```{r}
jags.1 <- run_model(run="test", mix, source, discr, model_filename)
```

```{r}
jags.1 <- run_model(run="very long", mix, source, discr, model_filename)
```

#22. Derive trophic position from % marine mix (Ramirez et al. values)

Derive the terrestrial beta value from herbivores, assuming they are TP2.

```{r}
T_herb <- Data %>%filter(category == "terrestrial_herbivore")
T_herb <- T_herb %>%filter(!common_name == "guinea pig" & !common_name == "armadillo"& !common_name == "coati")
T_herb <-  T_herb %>% rowwise() %>% mutate (beta = 7.6-(glu_d15N-phe_d15N) )
beta_T = mean(T_herb$beta)
sigma_beta_T = sd(T_herb$beta)
beta_T
sigma_beta_T
```

Calculate the uncertainties on trophic level estimates.

```{r}
# ---- Input Data ----
# Measured values
beta_M <- -3.3 #Marine beta value from  Ramirez et al.
beta_T <- 6.6 #Terrestrial beta value from Ramirez et al.
TDF <- 7.6  # Trophic discriminat factor from Ramirez

# Standard deviations from Ramirez
sigma_beta_M <- 1.8 # marine beta uncertainty
sigma_beta_T <- 3.4  # terrestrial beta uncertainty
sigma_TDF <- 1.1 # TDF uncertainty from Neilsen

# Partial derivatives for error propagation
Result_mix_TP <- Result_mix %>% rowwise() %>%
mutate(dTP_dGlu = ((1/TDF)^2)*(glu_d15Nstdev^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dPhe=((-1/TDF)^2)*(phe_d15Nstdev^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta=(((beta_M-beta_T)/TDF)^2)*(SD_marine^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta_T=(((Mean_terrestrial)/TDF)^2)*(sigma_beta_T^2))%>%mutate(dTP_dBeta_M=((Mean_marine/TDF)^2)*(sigma_beta_M^2))%>%mutate(dTP_sigma=(((-1/(TDF^2))*(glu_d15N-phe_d15N+((Mean_terrestrial)*beta_T)+(Mean_marine*beta_M)))^2)*(sigma_TDF^2))
```

```{r}
Result_mix_TP_final <- Result_mix_TP %>%
  rowwise() %>% mutate(Mix_TP = (((glu_d15N - phe_d15N) + (((Mean_marine)*beta_M) + ((Mean_terrestrial))*beta_T)) / TDF) + 1)%>% mutate(Mix_TP_sigma = (sqrt(dTP_dGlu + dTP_dPhe + dTP_dBeta +dTP_dBeta_T + dTP_dBeta_M + dTP_sigma)))
```

```{r}
humans_mix <- Result_mix_TP_final %>% filter(group == "Human", !is.na(Mean_marine), !is.na(d34S))

n_sim <- 10000
set.seed(1)
d34S_marine_by_site <- humans_mix %>% group_by(Site) %>% group_modify(~{
  if (nrow(.x) < 3) return(tibble(n = nrow(.x), r = NA, p = NA, r_lower = NA, r_upper = NA, p_lower = NA, p_upper = NA))
  sim <- replicate(n_sim, {
    marine_sim <- rnorm(nrow(.x), .x$Mean_marine, .x$SD_marine)
    c(r = cor(.x$d34S, marine_sim), p = cor.test(.x$d34S, marine_sim)$p.value)
  })
  tibble(
    n = nrow(.x),
    r = cor(.x$d34S, .x$Mean_marine, method = "pearson"),
    p = cor.test(.x$d34S, .x$Mean_marine, method = "pearson")$p.value,
    r_lower = quantile(sim["r", ], 0.025),
    r_upper = quantile(sim["r", ], 0.975),
    p_lower = quantile(sim["p", ], 0.025),
    p_upper = quantile(sim["p", ], 0.975)
  )
})
d34S_marine_by_site
cor.test(humans_mix$d34S, humans_mix$Mean_marine, method = "pearson")  # pooled, for comparison
```

```{r}
    tp_sim <- rnorm(nrow(.x), .x$Mix_TP, .x$Mix_TP_sigma)

    r = cor(.x$d34S, .x$Mix_TP, method = "pearson"),
```

```{r}
  labs(y=expression(delta^{15}*N[Gly]*"(‰)"), x=expression(delta^{15}*N[Phe]*"(‰)"))+
  scale_x_continuous(position="bottom", limits=c(0,20))+
  scale_y_continuous(position = "left", limits=c(0,20))+
  geom_point(data=fauna, aes(y=gly_d15N, x=phe_d15N, fill=category), colour="black", alpha=0.8, pch=23, size=4)+
  geom_point(data=humans, aes(y=gly_d15N, x=phe_d15N, fill=Site), colour="black",  alpha=0.8, pch=21, size=4)+
  # common_name labels dropped (overplotting at this density) - see Fig2a for labelled version
  scale_fill_manual(values=combined_cols, breaks=combined_order)+
    theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())+
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1)
Fig6a
```

#29. Save Fig6 (A-C)

```{r}
Fig6_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(Fig6c)
Fig6_top    <- cowplot::plot_grid(Fig6a + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                  Fig6b + theme(legend.position = "none"),
                                  labels = c("A", "B"), ncol = 2)
Fig6_bottom <- cowplot::plot_grid(Fig6c + theme(legend.position = "none"), Fig6_legend,
                                  labels = c("C", ""), ncol = 2)
Fig6 <- cowplot::plot_grid(Fig6_top, Fig6_bottom, nrow = 2)
Fig6
ggsave(here('figures','Fig6.svg'), width = 17.8, height = 17.8, dpi = 300, units = "cm", device='svg')
ggsave(here('figures','Fig6.pdf'), width = 17.8, height = 17.8, dpi = 300, units = "cm", device = cairo_pdf)
```
